data.long_meaning: The name Guhan means 'Cave' in Sanskrit, Telugu, Malayalam, Tamil, Kannada, and Bengali. It is derived from the Sanskrit word 'Guha' which means 'cave' or 'secret'. This name is associated with protection and secrecy, and is often given to children born in times of danger or uncertainty. The name Guhan carries the meaning “Cave” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Hindu tradition and is also used in Sanskrit, Telugu, Malayalam. Parents who choose Guhan usually hope their child will grow to embody cave and live with faith, good character and purpose.

This name is also associated with the legendary Hindu epic, the Mahabharata, where Bhishma Pitamaha (Grandfather Bhishma) is referred to as 'Guhai-Kshatriya', one who lives in a cave, signifying his noble character and strong will.
data.spiritual_significance: In Hinduism, the cave is symbolic of inner transformation and Self-realization. The name 'Guhan' is believed to imbue its bearer with the qualities of protection, secrecy, and hidden strength, much like how a cave shields its occupants from the outside world. It is also believed that the name instills a deep sense of inner calm and introspection, inspiring its bearer to delve deep within himself to unearth his inner wisdom and spiritual potential.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Guhan, in Hindu mythology, is the name of the secret cave where Lord Rama, the ideal man, lived in disguise with his wife Sita during his exile. It symbolizes the inner sanctum, the hidden soul, where one can find peace, protection and unity with the divine.
